pencereler.5-12: the night, a runaway oil train rolled into a Quebec town. Nobody was aboard. It had been parked uphill
pencereler.12-20: with too few handbrakes applied. A fire broke out on the locomotive. When the engine was shut down, its air brakes slowly
pencereler.20-30: released. The train began rolling down toward the town. Canada tightened rules for securing trains and building tank cars.

segmentler.metin: The Lac-Mégantic oil train rolled into town, derailed and exploded.
It took only too few handbrakes on an unattended train on a slope.
So how could too few handbrakes on an unattended train on a slope do this?
The answer is air brakes releasing after the locomotive was shut down, with insufficient handbrakes to hold the train — and it is why Canada tightened rules on securing trains and on tank car design.
